thresholdOverrides.reason: Byte-level container parsers mirror the JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, JUMBF, CBOR, DNG, OOXML, and ISO-BMFF specifications. Their branch count is format shape, not product branching; the reader and writer fixtures are the acceptance.
readFile walks one container once and prints the field list. Its branches follow the tag families the reader accepts; the reader fixtures are the acceptance.
sniffFormat is a flat signature table over the supported containers. Each branch names one magic number, so the count grows with the format list rather than product logic.
inspect decodes the TIFF, IFD, and DNG tag grammar of one container. Its branches follow the DNG specification; the DNG fixtures are the acceptance.
The cleaner, the worker, and the browser engine seam map one clean request to the engine state machine and its message shape. Their branches follow the engine protocol.
The writer ports translate one clean request into ExifTool arguments and errors. Their branching follows the tool's argument surface.
The session hook maps the named engine states to one page state. Splitting the state table across hooks would spread one switch across files.
The desk components print the report, the locator, the order, and the receipt from one report shape. Their cognitive load is the printed state table and the per-format preview branches.
The glyph atlas is written by a build script (bun brand:gen), not shipped runtime code, so it has no unit coverage. Its branches map OpenType path commands one-to-one.
The tabular engine mirrors the CSV, BIFF, OOXML, and SpreadsheetML grammars and one command set. Its branch count follows those formats, and the fixture plus branch tests are the acceptance.

The Tabular desk prints the parse, grid, dialog, and export states from one session shape. Components are E2E territory in this repo, so unit coverage is zero by design and CRAP reads complexity alone. The 26 browser tests and the recorded captures are the acceptance.

The route hook maps the named engine states to one page state and owns focus, selection, and clipboard recovery. Splitting that state table across hooks would spread one switch across files, as with use-expose. The browser tests are the acceptance.
parseText validates the strict CSV quote grammar before Papa Parse runs. Its branch count follows the delimited-text grammar, and the parser fixtures plus branch tests are the acceptance.
The PWA check waits on a live server built by the smoke job, so the retry loop has no unit coverage.
